info.description:
# Overview
Use this API to get HMRC Assist feedback about potential inaccuracies in returns before they are formally submitted.
You must follow a two-step process:
1. Send draft return data.
2. Use the relevant acknowledgement endpoint to confirm that your software has presented the HMRC Assist feedback messages to the user.

Because this process operates on draft, unfinalised data, requesting feedback carries no formal declaration. Also, the process does not block formal declaration submission via the *returns* endpoint of the [VAT (MTD) API](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/api-documentation/docs/api/service/vat-api/). Your software must allow customers to submit their VAT return, irrespective of any HMRC Assist submission feedback.

post.description:
Send VAT return data, to receive feedback from HMRC before formally submitting a VAT return. The response will contain feedback messages in English and Welsh, highlighting potential mistakes or discrepancies in the VAT return data. **Note:** Before using this endpoint, you must first call the obligations endpoint on the [VAT (MTD) API](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/api-documentation/docs/api/service/vat-api/) to get the period key. ### Test data

Scenario simulations using Gov-Test-Scenario headers are only available in the sandbox environment.

Header Value (Gov-Test-Scenario) Scenario

Default (No header value)

Simulates the scenario where there is one HMRC Assist feedback message.

MULTIPLE_FEEDBACK

Simulates the scenario where there are more than one HMRC VAT Assist feedback messages.

NO_FEEDBACK

Simulates the scenario where there is no HMRC VAT Assist feedback.

INVALID_VRN

Simulates the scenario where the VRN has not passed validation.

INVALID_PERIODKEY

Simulates the scenario where the periodKey has not passed validation.

INVALID_REQUEST

Submission has not passed validation. Invalid values.

TAX_PERIOD_NOT_ENDED

Simulates the scenario where the accounting period has not ended.

INSOLVENT_TRADER

Simulates the scenario where the client is an insolvent trader.

periodKey.description: The ID code for the period that this obligation belongs to. This should be obtained from the obligations endpoint of the [VAT (MTD) API](https://developer.service.hmrc.gov.uk/api-documentation/docs/api/service/vat-api/). The format is a string of four alphanumeric characters. Occasionally the format includes the # symbol.

vatDueSales.description: VAT due on sales and other outputs. This corresponds to box 1 on the VAT Return form.

vatDueAcquisitions.description: VAT due in the period on acquisitions of goods made in Northern Ireland from EU Member States. This corresponds to box 2 on the VAT Return form.

totalVatDue.description: Total VAT due (the sum of vatDueSales and vatDueAcquisitions). This corresponds to box 3 on the VAT Return form.

vatReclaimedCurrPeriod.description: VAT reclaimed in the period on purchases and other inputs (including acquisitions in Northern Ireland from EU member states). This corresponds to box 4 on the VAT Return form.

netVatDue.description:
The absolute difference between the *totalVatDue* and
*vatReclaimedCurrPeriod* values. This should therefore be a positive
number, calculated by subtracting the smallest value from the
largest. HMRC will automatically determine whether the number
represents net VAT that is due or net VAT that can be reclaimed.

This corresponds to box 5 on the VAT Return form.

totalValueSalesExVAT.description: Total value of sales and all other outputs excluding any VAT. This corresponds to box 6 on the VAT Return form. The value must be in whole pounds (no pence).

totalValuePurchasesExVAT.description: Total value of purchases and all other inputs excluding any VAT (including exempt purchases). This corresponds to box 7 on the VAT Return form. The value must be in whole pounds (no pence).

totalValueGoodsSuppliedExVAT.description: Total value of dispatches of goods and related costs (excluding VAT) from Northern Ireland to EU Member States. This corresponds to box 8 on the VAT Return form. The value must be in whole pounds (no pence).

totalAcquisitionsExVAT.description: Total value of acquisitions of goods and related costs (excluding VAT) made in Northern Ireland from EU Member States. This corresponds to box 9 on the VAT Return form. The value must be in whole pounds (no pence).

The scenario where there is one HMRC Assist feedback message.

Note that the feedback message in this example is for illustration purposes only. Actual feedback messages may differ.

englishFeedback.body: The VAT due on sales figure appears lower than expected based on your total sales value.
englishFeedback.title: HMRC feedback: VAT due on sales appears low

englishFeedback.description:
An array that contains up to 5 HMRC Assist feedback messages, in English.

The total number of characters across all text fields in an individual message will not exceed 32767.

itemNumber.description: The unique identifier for the feedback message. Corresponding English and Welsh feedback messages will have the same number.

title.description: The title of the feedback message. It tells the user to review or check something in the return.
title.example: VAT due on sales appears low

body.description: The main body of the feedback message, which is an explanation that usually consists of three or four sentences.
body.example: The VAT due on sales figure appears lower than expected based on your total sales value.

action.description: The recommended action (if any) that the customer should take to address the issue described in the feedback message.
action.example: Please review box 1 and box 6 of your VAT return.

links.description: A list of links to any supporting information that relates to the feedback message.

title.description: The title or brief description of the supporting information.

url.description: The URL of the supporting information.

path.description: The VAT box numbers and equivalent descriptions (as appearing on a paper return) that are the focus of the feedback presented in the message.
